recipe: Quick-pickle onion in lime juice and a pinch of salt, at least 15 min.
Heat beans with cumin, chili powder, salt. Mash slightly.
Fill with beans, avocado, pickled onion, cilantro, salsa.
recipe_detailed: Start the onions first: toss the sliced red onion with the lime juice and a big pinch of salt in a small bowl. Let it sit at least 15 min, stirring once or twice, until the onion turns bright pink and softens.

Warm the black beans in a skillet over medium with the cumin, chili powder, a pinch of salt, and a splash of water. Once they're hot, mash about a third of them with a fork or potato masher so the filling holds together in the tortilla.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high and warm the tortillas 30 seconds per side until soft and lightly spotted. Stack them in a clean towel to keep warm.
Slice the avocados. Fill each tortilla with beans, avocado, pickled onion, cilantro, and a spoonful of salsa. Drizzle a little of the pickling lime over the top.

set.tip2: Bloom the cumin, turmeric, and coriander in the oil for a full minute before the liquid goes in. Raw ground spices taste dusty; toasted ones give the broth its warm, earthy backbone.
recipe_detailed: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot over medium. Cook onion and carrots 5-6 min until the onion is soft and translucent. Add garlic and cook 1 min.
Add cumin, turmeric, and coriander. Stir for 30-60 seconds until fragrant. Add diced tomatoes, red lentils, and broth, and stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook 15-20 min, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are completely soft and have dissolved into the broth, thickening it.
Stir in the kale and cook 3 min until wilted. Squeeze lemon juice in at the end to brighten the whole pot, and season with salt and pepper.

set.tip2: Taste the cooked ground before it goes into the bowls. Plant-based ground is milder than beef, so it usually needs an extra pinch of salt and a squeeze of lime to taste like real taco meat.
recipe_detailed: Heat a large skillet over medium-high. Add the plant-based ground in an even layer and leave it alone for 2 min so the bottom browns. Then break it up and cook 3 more min until browned all over.
Add taco seasoning and 2 tbsp water. Stir 1 min until the water evaporates and the spices coat the crumbles. Taste and adjust with salt and a squeeze of lime.
Warm the black beans in a small pot with a splash of water and a pinch of salt. Mash a few against the side of the pot for a creamier texture.
Build bowls: chopped romaine, seasoned ground, beans, sliced avocado, and salsa. Finish with lime wedges for squeezing over the top.

set.tip2: Brown the Andouille well before anything else goes in the pot. The rendered fat is what you cook the trinity in, and it carries the smoky, spicy flavor through the whole dish.
recipe_detailed: Brown the sliced Andouille in a large pot over medium-high, 5 min, until the edges are crisp and the fat has rendered. Remove the sausage and leave the drippings in the pot.
Add the Holy Trinity (onion, celery, and bell pepper) to the drippings and cook 6 min until soft. Add garlic, thyme, smoked paprika, cayenne, and bay leaves and stir 1 min until fragrant.
Add the drained beans and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 min. Toward the end, smash some of the beans against the side of the pot until the sauce turns thick and creamy.
Return the sausage and simmer 5 more min. Remove the bay leaves and season with salt and pepper. Serve over rice with hot sauce and sliced green onion.

recipe_detailed: Bring the water or broth to a boil with a big pinch of salt. Pour in the polenta in a slow stream while whisking constantly so it doesn't clump. Turn the heat to low and stir 5 min, then cook 15-20 min, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until thick and creamy with no gritty bite.
Stir in the butter and most of the Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. If it thickens too much while you finish everything else, loosen it with a splash of hot water.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the sliced garlic and cook 1 min until fragrant but not browned. Add the spinach in handfuls, tossing until each batch wilts, 3-4 min total. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a small cup, then slide it into the water. Poach 3 min for runny yolks and lift out with a slotted spoon.
Spoon the polenta into shallow bowls, top with the spinach and a poached egg, and finish with the remaining Parmesan and cracked pepper.
